newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates end easy as gilts continue rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates end easy as gilts continue rally.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday unchanged at 0.1-0.25 percent while prices of government securities continued their rise, dealers said.
The market was range-bound between 0.10-0.25 percent thoughout the day with lenders outnumbering borrowers in a highly liquid market, they said.

"The call rates are expected to be in the region of 0.25-0.75 percent on Wednesday," a dealer said. "We expect the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)to mop up 30.0 billion rupees on Monday's repos auction at a cut-off rate of 3.90 percent."
The Bombay money market is closed on Tuesday as banks are closed for a local holiday.
The prices of securities continued their rally on Monday with prices rising by as high as 50 basis points for medium to long term paper, dealers said.
The medium term securities and treasury bills attracted heavy trading interest, they said.
The volume rose to 4.90 billion rupees on Monday, compared to previous 4.52 billion, dealers said.
